properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 3 at 9:19AM CDT until September 3 at 12:15PM CDT by NWS Milwaukee/Sullivan WI
properties.description:
FFWMKX

The National Weather Service in Milwaukee/Sullivan has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northern Milwaukee County in southeastern Wisconsin...
Southwestern Ozaukee County in southeastern Wisconsin...
Southeastern Washington County in southeastern Wisconsin...
Northeastern Waukesha County in southeastern Wisconsin...

* Until 1215 PM CDT.

* At 919 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Northern Milwaukee, Wauwatosa, Brookfield, Menomonee Falls, Mequon,
Whitefish Bay, Pewaukee, Brown Deer, Sussex, Fox Point, Bayside,
Thiensville, Germantown, Glendale, Butler, River Hills, Lannon,
Shorewood and Colgate.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 3 at 8:09AM CDT until September 3 at 10:00AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
FFWHGX

The National Weather Service in Houston/Galveston has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Houston County in southeastern Texas...
Northeastern Trinity County in southeastern Texas...

* Until 1000 AM CDT.

* At 809 AM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
4 and 6 inches of rain have fallen. Rainfall rates are 1 to 2
inches per hour at times. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5
inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Apple Springs, Groveton, Kennard, Centralia, Pennington and Weches.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
